item.title: Sextans B
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: A Local Group irregular on the group's outer rim — one of the most distant dwarf galaxies bound to our neighborhood.

item.title: Sextans Dwarf Spheroidal
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: A very faint Milky Way satellite 290,000 light-years out — one of the least luminous dwarf spheroidals in the halo.

item.title: Shapley Supercluster
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The Shapley Concentration — the heaviest nearby supercluster, ~650 Mly out, containing ~8,000 galaxies.

item.title: Sirius B
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The Pup — the first white dwarf ever recognized, orbiting the sky's brightest star.

item.title: Sirius
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The Dog Star — brightest star in Earth's night sky, hiding a dead companion.

item.title: Small Magellanic Cloud
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The Milky Way's second satellite — a metal-poor dwarf galaxy being slowly torn apart.

item.title: Sun
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The G-type main-sequence star holding 99.86% of the Solar System's mass.

item.title: Tarantula Nebula
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The most violent star-forming region in the Local Group — in a satellite galaxy 160,000 ly away.

item.title: Tau Ceti e
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: A super-Earth in the nearest single-star habitable zone — one of the quietest Sun-like hosts.

item.title: Tau Ceti f
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The cold outer candidate — a heavy super-Earth on the habitable zone's far rim.

item.title: Tau Ceti
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: A quiet Sun-like star 12 light-years away with a crowded inner system.

item.title: Titan
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The only moon with a thick atmosphere — methane rivers, lakes and rain on a frozen water-ice world.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: Seven Earth-size worlds around a star barely bigger than Jupiter.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1b
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The innermost of the seven resonant worlds — a scorched Earth-size rock.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1c
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: Venus-mass sibling orbiting in the inner warmth of the resonant chain.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1d
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The lightest of the seven — a sub-Earth-mass world at the warmth's edge.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1e
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The densest Earth-analog of the seven — the system's best shot at liquid water.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1f
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: A water-rich world on the habitable zone's inner edge.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1g
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The largest of the seven — a cool super-Earth at the chain's outer anchor.

item.title: TRAPPIST-1h
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The cold outer edge — the system's ice-cloaked final world.

item.title: Triangulum Galaxy
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The quiet third spiral — the Local Group's shy member, rich in star nurseries.

item.title: Triton
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: Neptune's captured moon — a Kuiper-belt world with nitrogen geysers, orbiting backwards.

item.title: Tucana Dwarf
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The Local Group's most isolated spheroidal — 2.9 Mly out, never influenced by a major galaxy.

item.title: Ursa Major I Dwarf
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: An ultra-faint Milky Way satellite found by SDSS — a dark-matter domination showcase at the edge of galaxy formation.

item.title: Ursa Major II Dwarf
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: One of the faintest galaxies known — an ultra-faint Milky Way satellite only ~105,000 light-years out.

item.title: Uranus
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The sideways planet — an ice giant rolling around the Sun on its side.

item.title: Ursa Minor Dwarf
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: A Milky Way spheroid 225,000 light-years out — ancient, faint, and nearly all dark matter.

item.title: Vega
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The former and future North Star — astronomy's zero-point of brightness.

item.title: Venus
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: Earth's twin in size, wrapped in a crushing CO₂ greenhouse — the hottest planet.

item.title: Vesta
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The asteroid belt's brightest world — a protoplanet that survived the dawn of the Solar System.

item.title: Virgo Supercluster
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: The Local Supercluster — a flattened cloud of ~100 galaxy groups centred on the Virgo Cluster ~54 Mly away.

item.title: WLM Galaxy
item.dc:creator: Luis Krötz
item.description: Wolf–Lundmark–Melotte — an isolated irregular with its own globular cluster, 3 Mly from home.
